extracted.intended_audience: State and Federal Health Insurance Exchanges, QHP issuers, agents/brokers/web-brokers, navigators/assisters, and other marketplace stakeholders and commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of proposed regulatory requirements and evaluative criteria in HHS/CMS proposed rulemaking concerning Exchange verification, income documentation, premium payment thresholds, and special enrollment provisions for plan years 2027 and beyond. Targets rules and operational expectations for Exchanges, issuers, and enrollment assistors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-enrollment verification implementation timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges must establish a pre-enrollment verification process no later than August 1, 2027 (requirement derived from section 71303 of the WFTC legislation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS seeks comment on operational considerations and the timelines required to comply with this law including impacts on State Exchanges, issuers, agents/brokers, navigators/assisters, and consumers; commenters should consider anticipated complexity, costs, burdens, and enrollment impacts. This is a statutory deadline tied to implementation of section 71303 of WFTC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income verification when trusted data indicate income <100% FPL (§155.320(c)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Require submission of documents to verify income when an applicant attests projected household income at or above 100 percent of the FPL but trusted data sources indicate household income is below 100 percent of the FPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy was finalized in the 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability rule and is proposed to continue because HHS assessed these verifications as necessary to prevent improper enrollments and improper APTC payments and to guard against agent/broker/web-broker misconduct (including AI impersonation). HHS views documentation submission as reasonable, necessary, and not unduly burdensome and notes potential program integrity savings outweigh operational costs. If unverified, a DMI may lead to loss of APTC after the 90-day DMI period; documentation also protects consumers from accumulating tax liabilities given changes to repayment caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set a 90-day inconsistency (DMI) period per section 1411(e)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges must set a 90-day inconsistency period (DMI) in instances where an applicant's attested annual household income cannot be verified by data sources, allowing applicants the opportunity to present satisfactory documentary evidence or resolve the inconsistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows section 1411(e)(4) of the Affordable Care Act and HHS proposes this requirement for verifications of eligibility for 2027 coverage and beyond. If the inconsistency remains unresolved after the 90-day period, Exchanges would generally deny eligibility for APTC and CSRs (and in practice result in loss of APTC). HHS proposes that Federal platform Exchanges would implement procedures in §155.315(f)(1)-(4) to create annual income DMIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification using trusted data sources and procedures under section 1411(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges must verify income information using trusted data sources under section 1411(d) when IRS data are unavailable or when 'changes in circumstances' are indicated; accepting attestation alone is insufficient when verification authority applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS interprets section 1411(d) to require verification of information not submitted to Treasury (including changes in circumstances). When IRS data are unavailable, Exchanges should proceed to further verification using established verification processes for annual income rather than accepting attestation. This includes comparing projected annual income to IRS data (when available) within thresholds to determine whether a change in circumstance exists per section 1412(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind acceptance of attestations when IRS returns no data (§155.320(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the requirement that Exchanges accept an applicant's household income attestation when the IRS returns no tax data in response to verification requests; beginning with PY2027, Exchanges must collect documentation from applicants when IRS returns no data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS proposes permanently rescinding §155.320(c)(5), reversing the temporary pause that allowed acceptance of attestations where IRS returned no data. The agency explains prior reasoning for the temporary policy and now concludes the statutory framework and program integrity/tax liability considerations warrant verification beyond attestation. Exchanges should check other data sources and use the 90-day DMI process when IRS returns no data; failure to verify may lead to denial of APTC and CSRs after the DMI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow statutory APTC determination process (compare projected income to IRS data; use 1412(b)(2) when change in circumstance)
rubrics_metrics.description: When IRS data are provided, Exchanges should compare an applicant's projected annual household income to IRS data (within thresholds) to determine alignment or a change in circumstance; if a change in circumstance is found, the Exchange may determine APTC using projected income per section 1412(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains the methodology for determining APTC under sections 1411(c), 1411(d), and 1412(b)(2) — relying on IRS data for the second preceding year unless there is a change in circumstance, in which case projected income can be used. If neither IRS nor other trusted data can verify income, Exchanges must follow 1411(e)(4) procedures (reasonable efforts, contact applicant, 90-day opportunity to present evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require documentation and deny APTC/CSRs if verification fails (protect consumers from tax liabilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: When verification against trusted data sources fails or IRS returns no data, Exchanges should require documentary verification; if applicants do not verify within the DMI period, they will lose APTC and CSRs, which protects applicants from accumulating excess APTC tax liabilities given removal of repayment caps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS emphasizes that ending repayment caps under section 71305 of the WFTC legislation (effective PY2026) increases the importance of documentation to prevent consumers from incurring large tax liabilities due to misestimated or misreported income. The proposed policy would halt APTC for consumers who cannot verify income with documentation after 90 days to avoid large future tax repayment obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced scrutiny for assisted enrollments (agents/brokers/web-brokers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply increased verification scrutiny to applications assisted by agents, brokers, and web-brokers, given evidence these channels have been associated with higher rates of improper enrollments and income misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS cites internal data showing nearly 80 percent of income DMIs were generated for households assisted by agents/brokers/web-brokers in PY2024, GAO findings showing vulnerabilities exploited by assistors, and reports of AI-enabled impersonation of consumers. The agency proposes continued and possibly heightened verification measures targeted at these assisted enrollments to protect program integrity and consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment solicitation: discontinue fixed-dollar and gross percentage premium payment thresholds (§155.400)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit comment on whether HHS should permanently discontinue regulatory options allowing QHP issuers to implement fixed-dollar and gross percentage-based premium payment thresholds for PY2027 and beyond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: The 2026 Payment Notice allowed a fixed-dollar threshold (up to $10 adjusted for inflation) and a gross percentage-based threshold (e.g., 98% of gross premium). HHS paused these options through PY2026 due to program integrity concerns associated with enhanced subsidies. HHS explains that fixed-dollar and gross percentage thresholds may enable consumers to remain unknowingly enrolled and allow improper enrollments to persist by avoiding notices that would otherwise alert consumers. HHS seeks comment on whether to let the options sunset, rescind them for a fixed period, or permanently rescind, considering tradeoffs for low-income consumers and consumers with chronic conditions who may benefit from flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider State Exchange flexibility to adopt premium thresholds even if Federal platform disallows them
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit comment on whether it would be appropriate to grant State Exchanges flexibility to adopt fixed-dollar and/or gross percentage premium payment thresholds even if those options remain unavailable for Exchanges on the Federal platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS acknowledges State-specific variation in improper enrollment risk and stakeholder comments that limiting flexibility was unnecessary in some State Exchanges with lower improper enrollment rates. The agency requests input on whether to allow State Exchanges to implement one or both thresholds as a tailored option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend removal of 150 percent FPL SEP beyond PY2026 (§155.420(d)(16))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.420(d)(16) so that all Exchanges will continue to be prohibited from offering the 150 percent FPL special enrollment period (SEP) after PY2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 150 percent FPL SEP previously allowed monthly SEP enrollment at the Exchange's option for individuals eligible for APTC with household income no greater than 150% FPL. HHS proposes conforming amendments to remove related regulatory cross-references (§155.420(a)(4)(ii)(D) and 155.420(b)(2)(vii)) and revise §155.420(a)(4)(iii). The proposal is to align regulations with section 71304 of the WFTC legislation and is based on balancing access objectives with program integrity concerns.
